item.title: The President's Cake | Arthouse Now — Fri Oct 23, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
While people struggle daily to survive under sanctions in Saddam’s Iraq, nine-year-old Lamia must use her wits to gather ingredients for the mandatory cake to celebrate President Saddam Hussein’s birthday or face the consequences—prison or death. A touching coming-of-age tale that combines empathy, pragmatism, universally relatable characters, and striking cinematography. [105 min; drama; Arabic with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: The Robert Cray Band — Fri Oct 23, 7:30 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Blues icon. Soul man. Rock and roller. Robert Cray is all these things and more.
The Georgia born, Washington raised musician first picked up a guitar after seeing The Beatles on TV then, having witnessed Jimi Hendrix perform in Seattle, determined that his destiny would also follow a similar path. And so he has: across the past half century Robert Cray’s developed into one of American music’s most singular artists.
Across five decades Robert Cray has created a richly inclusive American music, revitalizing both blues and soul while rocking hard with the very best. To achieve 50 years in the music industry and still be as fresh and committed as when starting out is an achievement few can boast of but Cray can: he has released 19 studio albums, every one replete with his extremely distinctive songs, won five Grammy Awards and continues to make music that sounds like no one but Robert Cray.
PRESENTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH AMETHYST HOUSE Amethyst House is a nonprofit organization based in

item.title: Don't Look Now | Friday Night Frights — Fri Oct 23, 10:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description: Adapted from a Daphne du Maurier short story, Don't Look Now follows John (Donald Sutherland) and Christine (Julie Christie), still grieving over the accidental death of their daughter, as they head to Venice for John's work restoring a church. Soon, Laura meets two sisters who claim to be in touch with the spirit of their dead daughter and the couple must decide what is real, what is supernatural, and what is somewhere in-between. Renowned for innovative editing style, memorable recurring aesthetic motifs, an impressionistic formal style, and nonlinear storytelling that destabilizes the viewer, the film was controversial on its release but is now considered a classic, landing multiples times on Sight and Sound’s list of the best films of all time, the BFI list of greatest British films, and was reevaluated by Roget Ebert as an occult-horror classic. Don’t Look Now has also inspired filmmakers like Danny Boyle, Lynne Ramsey, Ari Aster, Steven Soderbergh, and many more. [110 min; horror

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Pythagoean Theorem Day — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Wonderlab
item.description:
Blow your mind at WonderLab this Pythagorean Theorem Day! Explore hands-on triangle challenges, math-inspired art, and puzzles throughout the museum, and discover how one ancient theorem still shows up everywhere - from architecture to nature to the numbers on today's calendar.Fun Fact: Pythagoras was kind of a radical dude in his day - he ran a secret society of math-obsessed mystics, believed numbers held the key to the universe, and mixed geometry with music, philosophy, and a little bit of showmanship. For Pythagoras, math was mind-blowing.Embrace the endless creativity of mathematics. Join us at WonderLab for Pythagorean Theorem Day - a once-in-a-lifetime date when the calendar does the math for you: 10-24-26 means 10² \+ 24² = 26².
Source: Limestone Post

item.description:
BLOOMINGTON BOOK FEST: WRIGHT THOMPSON Join the Bloomington Book Festival for the third annual presentation of the Bob Hammel Writing Award.
The 2026 winner and keynote speaker is Wright Thompson, a New York Times-bestselling author and revered journalist. A native of Clarksdale, in the Mississippi Delta, Thompson has spent two decades proving that the best stories are often about ambition, loss, family, and the price of greatness.
His latest book, The Barn: The Secret History of a Murder in Mississippi, is a haunting account of the brutal 1955 murder of Emmett Till, named a Best Book of the Year by the Washington Post, TIME, and Vanity Fair, and nominated for a PEN America Literary Award.

item.title: Pie a Cowgirl — Mon Oct 26, 2:00 PM — Dunn Meadow 3 (Small event or tabling)
item.description: The "Pie a Cowgirl" is a fundraising event open to the public for the Western Equestrian Team at IU, with the purpose of raising funds for the team's use. Being an equestrian group, some of our most valuable teammates are our horses, which need round-the-clock care. We are responsible for their health and well-being. We prioritize the entire team learning the basic processes of equine hospitality. We are raising money to help cover some steep costs associated with our non-profit. Horse care costs a lot, including feeding, grooming, vet bills, transportation, and barn boarding, which can be a couple hundred dollars per horse per month. Horse care costs don't include the expenses incurred during the season for the rest of the team. We have other costs, such as travel expenses, competition attire purchases, event food expenses, and more. item.title: McCalla Center Open Gallery Hours — Tue Oct 27, 11:00 AM — McCalla Center
item.description: Outfitting IU Athletics: Hoosier Champions This exhibit showcases objects from IU's championship teams and athletes, connecting them to historic achievements in the Big Ten and the national stage. The items featured in the exhibit are from the IU Athletics Sports Memorabilia Collection and feature photos and videos provided by IU Athletics and Indiana University Archives. Dates: November 14, 2025 - October 2026 By Their Own Hands: The Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame! Founded in 1974 by the Culture and Ethnic Affairs Guild of the Oakland Museum of California, the Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame began as a film lecture series and awards ceremony celebrating achievements of Black film industry figures. When that organization closed, they donated their materials to IU. item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Wed Oct 28 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Oct 28 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. Whether you're curious about accommodations, have questions about the process, or simply want to learn more about available resources, we invite you to stop by and chat with Kade about the support options that may be available to you. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Oct 30, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Oct 30, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
